article.story: NEW YORK -- — Brandon Hagel scored two goals with less than two minutes to play to complete his hat trick and the Tampa Bay Lightning extended their winning streak to four games with a 5-3 victory over the New York Islanders on Saturday night. Hagel, who also had an assist, scored the go-ahead goal with 1:44 remaining and an empty-net goal 21 seconds later. Jake Guentzel scored twice for Tampa Bay, Andrei Vasilevskiy made 20 saves and the Lightning won the first half of their brief two-game New York road trip. Tony DeAngelo, Matthew Schaefer and Brayden Schenn scored for the Islanders. Ilya Sorokin finished with 21 saves. The Islanders erased a two-goal deficit in the second half of the second period to tie the score at 3. Schaefer used his skating to evade Anthony Cirelli along the blue line and create a shooting lane before firing a shot past Vasilevskiy to pull the Islanders within one. In the final seconds of the period, Schenn attempted a cross-ice pass to Kyle Palmieri at the back post, but the puck deflected off Lightning defenseman Erik Cernak and into the net for a power-play goal that tied it at 3. Guentzel opened the scoring 5:45 into the first period. Hagel doubled Tampa Bay’s lead with less than five minutes remaining in the first, skating past Ryan Pulock and converting a breakaway. DeAngelo pulled the Islanders within one at 6:27 of the second period with his first goal of the season, sending a wrist shot from the point over Vasilevskiy’s glove. Guentzel scored his second of the game on the power play to give the Lightning a 3-1 lead. Islanders defenseman Logan Stanley and Lightning forward Pontus Holmberg fought in the second period. Up next Lightning: Visit New York Rangers on Tuesday night. Islanders: Host the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NHL coverage here
